# Golden K-quant encoder vectors, produced by running llama.cpp's C encoders verbatim.
#
# Source functions (all copied unmodified into the generator harness):
#   nearest_int, make_qx_quants, make_q3_quants, make_qkx2_quants,
#   get_scale_min_k4, quantize_row_q{2,3,4,5,6}_K_ref,
#   quantize_row_q{4_0,5_0,5_1,8_0}_ref, dequantize_row_q{4,5,6}_K,
#   ggml_compute_fp32_to_fp16 / ggml_compute_fp16_to_fp32
# from  llama.cpp  commit ba7e817ee:
#   ggml/src/ggml-quants.c, ggml/src/ggml-impl.h, ggml/src/ggml-common.h
#
# Build command used to produce this file (the flags matter -- see below):
#   clang -O2 -std=c11 -DNDEBUG -ffp-contract=off -fno-fast-math oracle_kquant.c -lm
#
# -ffp-contract=off is required.  With clang's default contraction on aarch64 the
# accumulator updates `sumlx += w*x[i]*l` fuse into fmadd, which Rust never emits;
# the fused build disagrees with this file on 38 of the 84 Q2_K bytes of the
# `all_positive` case.  Verified: -O0 and -O2 with contraction off produce
# byte-identical output.
#
# Format, one record per case:
#   CASE <name> <n_elements>
#   IN      <n*8 hex chars>       f32 input, little-endian bit patterns
#   Q4K/Q5K/Q6K/Q2K/Q3K  <hex>    encoder output bytes (empty when n < 256)
#   Q40/Q80/Q50/Q51      <hex>    legacy encoder output bytes (controls)
#   RT_Q4K/RT_Q5K/RT_Q6K <hex>    f32 bit patterns after encode -> ggml decode
#   END
#
# The fp16_sweep record instead carries F16IN (f32 bits), F16OUT (fp16 bits) and
# F16BACK (f32 bits after a round trip), pinning `half::f16` to ggml's converter.

CASE lcg_mixed 512
IN 
Q4K 
Q5K 
Q6K 
Q2K 
Q3K 
Q40 
Q80 
Q50 
Q51 
RT_Q4K 
RT_Q5K 
RT_Q6K 
END
